title: atlantic-vpc-preflight-sketch-diego-ramos
content:
Context:
Personal prep notes for the Atlantic (customer) VPC/on-prem preflight. This is a scratchpad for the 1:1 + cross-team preflight meeting with CS/NetEng/Infra to get us ready for the alpha cutover window.

Meeting goal (30–45m):
- Surface live blockers blocking cutover readiness
- Confirm owners and short remediation timelines for each critical item
- Lock acceptance criteria for canary traffic and rollback triggers

Attendees (planned):
- Diego Ramos (me) - Redwood eng lead (onprem runtime)
- Priya Nair - Customer Success (Atlantic)
- Omar Haddad - NetEng (customer side contact)
- Lucia Chen - Infra Ops (Redwood Dedicated)
- Aaron Park - Customer SRE (Atlantic) - optional

Agenda rough:
1) Quick status (2m)
2) Milestone checklist (10m) — what is green/yellow/red
3) Blockers deep-dive (15m) — owners + quick fixes + risk
4) Cutover acceptance & rollback criteria (8m)
5) Action items + next sync (5m)

Milestone tracker (short form):
- VPC peering complete: target 2026-03-18 — owner: Omar Haddad — status: yellow (routing for subnets 10.4.0.0/16 not validated)
- KMS/HSM key exchange tested: target 2026-03-10 — owner: Priya Nair — status: green (test vector OK)
- Onprem package install validated on perf node: target 2026-03-12 — owner: Diego Ramos — status: yellow (OOM observed at 4k tokens)
- Network ACLs & egress: target 2026-03-15 — owner: Lucia Chen — status: red (egress policy blocks registry access)
- Monitoring / alert hooks in place: target 2026-03-16 — owner: Diego Ramos & Lucia Chen — status: yellow (metric names agreed, alert thresholds TBD)

Current blockers (inspection notes):
1) Container image pull failures from customer network (severity: high)
   - Symptom: nodes cannot fetch image from our artifact registry intermittently.
   - Immediate mitigation: provide a hosted mirror URL (secure presigned) and test pull (owner: Lucia).
   - Long term: adjust customer egress rules or push to their internal registry (owner: Omar).
   - Jira: JIRA-ONPREM-842

2) KV-cache warmup causing memory spikes (severity: med-high)
   - Observed OOM on small perf node when priming large prompt set (4k+ tokens).
   - Hypothesis: default cache size tuned for cloud not onprem smaller nodes.
   - Action: experiment with cache_size=0.6x and reduced batch_size; run two perf passes with heatmap (owner: Diego) — due 2026-03-09 (in practice slipped, need new due date).

3) Egress blocked for container runtime to our model-registry (severity: critical)
   - Cause: ACL denies outbound to S3 endpoints used for quantized artifacts.
   - Workaround: pre-bake artifacts into node image (temporary) or use customer-hosted mirror.
   - Who to escalate to: Atlantic network ops (Aaron), Redwood infra (Lucia).

4) TLS client cert rotation automation not installed (severity: low-med)
   - Manual cert upload required today; automation will be delivered after cutover. Acceptable if owner signs off.

Acceptance criteria for alpha (canary) traffic:
- 95p latency < 180ms for short prompts (< 512 tokens) over 30-minute steady state
- No more than 0.5% error rate (5xx / connection failures) for 1000 canary requests
- KV warmup memory usage stable (no OOMs) for 10k token consolidation tests
- Alerts firing correctly on CPU/GPU temperature and token error rate thresholds

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Sustained 5xx rate > 1% for 10 minutes
- Latency 95p > 400ms for 5 minutes
- Any OOM observed on production nodes during canary window

Action items (concrete, owner, due):
- Lucia: generate presigned mirror for image pull + smoke test logs (due 2026-03-12)
- Omar: open ACL exception ticket with Atlantic NetOps and confirm allowed endpoints (due 2026-03-13)
- Diego: run KV-cache tuning experiments (cache_size and batch_size matrix), attach memprof output + perf.log (new due 2026-03-14)
- Priya: confirm customer point-of-contact for rollback approval and their phone escalation chain (due 2026-03-11)
- Diego + Lucia: draft cutover runbook steps (1-page playbook + checklist) and store in confluence link (due 2026-03-15)
- All: short 15m sync day before cutover to confirm green flags (meeting planned 2026-03-17)

Preflight checklist (quick to run before sync):
- Can you curl the artifact S3 endpoint from a bastion? (cmd: curl -I https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/atlantic/manifest.json)
- Container pull: docker pull <mirror-url> (check sha256)
- Node free memory: free -h / dmesg | grep -i oom
- GPU health: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv
- Service logs: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep -i error

Notes for the meeting (things to call out verbally):
- Emphasize we can accept short manual steps today (e.g., pre-baked image) if they reduce risk, but we must have a plan to automate within two sprints.
- Ask customer if they will allow temporary increase to node size in the cutover window to reduce memory pressure (we can scale down later).
- Get explicit sign-off on rollback owner and point-in-time snapshot strategy for config rollback (who performs config revert?).

Risks not yet mitigated:
- Customer org policy might block presigned links (legal review). Owner: Priya (check).
- Nightly backup windows overlap with cutover (backup throttle could cause DB latency spikes). Owner: Aaron to confirm maintenance windows.

Follow-up notes (after meeting template):
- Record decisions inline (replicate to confluence runbook)
- Update milestone tracker with new dates + owners
- If presigned mirror works, tag the image and update install docs with mirror URL and sha256

Misc troubleshooting snippets (copy into terminal if needed):
- Check image pull verbose: docker --log-level=debug pull <mirror-url> 2>&1 | tee pull-debug.log
- Memory profiling on node: sudo cgroup-attach && cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/redwood/runtime/memory.stat

Personal TODOs (private):
- Reproduce OOM locally on 2 small node VMs (start 2026-03-09 morning)
- Draft short email to Atlantic ops summarizing remaining open items (send after meeting)

Next sync: 2026-03-17 09:00 PT (15m) - day-before cutover quick go/no-go

-- Diego
